answer: Edge-Disjoint Path Quota. Each agent must continuously sustain at least three independent routes to distinct known agents, each route requiring a locally verified round-trip through a different network neighborhood. To forge a sybil cluster, an attacker must provision real, geographically separated relays—no shortcut through cheap duplication. Every extra identity pays a copper-level cost in relay hardware and latency overhead per fresh route, making a large swath impractical. A single voyage of a new node earns it only provisional links until real cross-neighborhood traffic accumulates.
